speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The symptoms of stridor and wheezing that worsen with crying, feeding, and neck flexion are classic for this condition, along with the associated feeding intolerance and vomiting. Given the clinical presentation is highly specific, no further tests are required.
